name: James Ensor
findings: Uses greyish white 6.2x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 795 paintings here).
Uses olive-buff 4.7x more than the other paintings from the same museum(s), so camera and varnish are held equal (from 795 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, seal brown turns up as a small accent in 36% of the paintings that hold it, 2.0x the archive's rate (from 795 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, blue slate turns up as the lightest note in 50% of the paintings that hold it, 2.0x the archive's rate (from 795 paintings here).
Within his own canvases, chestnut turns up as the shadow in 80% of the paintings that hold it, 4.6x the archive's rate (from 795 paintings here).
Rarely uses smoky black, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 795 paintings here).
Rarely uses dark olive brown, common in the same museum(s)' other paintings (from 795 paintings here).
Pairs fawn with pale blush more than chance would predict (3 of 795 paintings here).
